target_customer: Parents paying a membership for on-demand pediatric telehealth, later health plans and employers (Carrot, Aetna Better Health of Illinois)
problem: Parents struggle to reach a pediatrician quickly and often end up in urgent care or the emergency room for illnesses a clinician could handle at home with diagnostics.
business_model: Consumer membership plus B2B2C contracts with health plans and employer benefit platforms
product_category: Pediatric telehealth with at-home diagnostic kits

founders.name: Harrison Gordon
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page; background not found in opened sources. Company release dated 2025-08-19 calls him co-founder and says he moved from CEO to President.

technical_complexity.rationale: Telehealth video and scheduling are standard; the harder parts were shipping at-home diagnostic devices, clinician staffing across states and clinical protocols.

defensibility.rationale: Licensed physician network and diagnostic kits take effort, but general telemedicine providers and pediatric practices could add similar offerings.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found as of 2026; the company stayed independent and in August 2025 added executives from MDLive and Teladoc.

market_need_then: The company claims general telemedicine refers children to urgent care and ER about three times as often as needed; independent demand evidence at founding was not found.

branding.domain_note: Uses blueberrypediatrics.com (descriptive exact name plus category word).

brand_strength.rationale: A friendly, memorable fruit name that fits a children's product; legal entity is sparkMD Inc operating as Blueberry Pediatrics. Little third-party press about the brand itself was found.

outcome_analysis: Blueberry Pediatrics remains an operating pediatric telehealth company that moved from consumer memberships toward health plans and employers, with partnerships such as Carrot and a leadership overhaul in August 2025. Funding is only visible on aggregators with conflicting totals, so the scale of its success cannot be judged.
notes: Funding unverified, only aggregators seen: CB Insights says about 12.1M over 7 rounds with a Series A dated 2023-03 and MS&AD Ventures; Seedtable and Caplight date a Series A to 2022-01 (about 9.3M); VCBacked says about 4M seed. These conflict, so no round is recorded. The WVV Capital Medium post about an investment was blocked (403). No dated 2018 competitor sources found, so the list is empty.
